stem: Why should a child with strabismus such as exotropia or esotropia have a thorough ocular examination?

options.text: It is always a normal variation that resolves on its own
It may be the presenting sign of an underlying intraocular pathology like retinoblastoma
It is purely a cosmetic issue that does not affect vision
It indicates the child needs immediate eye muscle surgery
It confirms the child has conjunctivitis

explanation: Intraocular pathology may present with strabismus, so a thorough ocular examination is needed to look for serious causes such as retinoblastoma.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because strabismus is not always benign and can be a sign of reduced vision or serious eye disease.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because strabismus can be the first sign of an underlying intraocular pathology such as retinoblastoma.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because strabismus can reflect abnormal visual input or ocular disease, not just a cosmetic concern.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the priority is to identify the underlying cause before considering treatment such as surgery.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because conjunctivitis does not explain strabismus and does not replace a full ocular examination.

source.hint: Recall the story of the little boy whose 'beauty spot' was actually a malignant tumor.
